detailedSummary: Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 supplies energy, finite-energy MA, locality, comparison and downward energy differentiation without smoothness. General surjectivity is equivalent to the envelope property (Theorem 12.8), which also implies unibranchness (Theorem 5.12). text:
The exact saved source Boucksom–Jonsson, Global pluripotential theory over a trivially valued field, arXiv:1801.08229v4, works over an algebraically closed trivially valued field. For integral projective X and ample L, let V=(L^n). Its normalized energy satisfies E(0)=0 and E(φ+c)=E(φ)+c. Its operator is probability-normalized; the genuine raw operator is V MA. The raw measure condition is μ(X^an)=V and sup_{φ∈E¹}[E(φ)−V⁻¹∫φ dμ]<∞.

Theorem 7.18 and Proposition 7.19 construct finite-energy MA, decreasing continuity, raw mass and normalization pushforward on possibly singular X. Theorems 7.40/7.44 give locality and comparison. Theorem 8.5 and Corollary 8.6 differentiate downward energy; identifying that energy with energy of a psh envelope requires envelope regularity.

Theorem A gives an embedding with dense image, with unconditional surjectivity when X is smooth and either characteristic is zero or dimension is at most two. Theorem 12.8 equates surjectivity with the envelope property; Theorem 5.11 equates envelopes with weak compactness. Theorem 5.12 makes unibranchness necessary. Conjecture 5.14 proposes the envelope property for unibranch varieties. Lemma 5.13 assumes envelope properties on classes approaching the target class, so it cannot establish those same properties by normalization.

The exact background inputs for the curve proof below are Example 2.5 (flag-ideal PL functions on singular X), Example 2.6 (ray generators on smooth curves), Proposition 3.6(vi) (nef reflection for an already descended target PL function), Proposition 3.10 (uniform ample-model approximation in a fixed ample class), Theorem 4.15(iii) and decreasing closure, Example 4.13 (smooth-curve slope criterion), Theorem 5.20 and Lemma 5.17 (smooth envelopes and continuity), Proposition 7.2, equation (7.5) (energy projection), Proposition 7.19, equation (7.18) (genuine MA projection), and Proposition 12.7 (strong continuity). Every new normalization application is proved in n2.

The supplied 1201.0188 PDF is actual v1. Its watermark is 30 December 2011 although its internal date is 29 October 2018; neither was silently relabelled. Theorem A assumes complete discrete valuation, residue characteristic zero, smooth projective X admitting descent to a one-variable function field completed by K, ample L, raw mass deg_L X, and support on the dual complex of an SNC model. L need not descend. This v1 is not an arbitrary-support finite-energy theorem. The supplied 1201.0187v2 similarly retains smooth projective, discretely valued, residue-characteristic-zero hypotheses for compactness and regularization.

1805.01016v3 is Boucksom–Eriksson, Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. Its Theorem A concerns continuous psh metrics on geometrically reduced projective schemes; Corollary B retains continuity of envelopes. Its continuous energy projection formula is not a finite-energy singular equation theorem. Synthetic 2307.01697v1, Theorem A, establishes density and completeness on the measure side, not actual-potential surjectivity. Pille–Schneider 2209.04879v2, Remark 4.4, distinguishes arbitrary-field finite-energy spaces from the unknown general extended operator. Gubler–Rabinoff 2506.13548v2 explicitly excludes constructing MA from that paper's singular-curve subharmonic results.

All ten authorized source-cache hashes match the supplied hashes. Twenty-one literal extracts, published proof passages, precise application checks and five fresh PDF-page extractions are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Saved PDF page 35 was visually checked for Proposition 3.6(vi) and its proof. Run python3 init_workspace.py and python3 provenance.py to reproduce the inventory and extracts. These checks establish provenance, not mathematical correctness. No assertion is made about every later source outside the authorized caches.

detailedSummary: Actual point ideals on singular X isolate normalization rays after division by their integer orders. This proves PL descent; model-nef reflection then proves psh descent without assuming envelopes on X. Finite normalization preserves the ample degree and energy. Actual-X finite-energy MA is therefore the root-plus-Stieltjes measure, with inverse obtained by integrating measure tails. Squared-tail finiteness is exactly the dual energy condition, excludes endpoint mass, and gives uniqueness modulo one constant. Compactness and envelopes transfer only after the cone isomorphism is proved. Envelope differentiation, comparison, approximation, strong continuity and bounded-reference dependence are checked. The result restricts dimension to one and uses the trivial valuation endpoint.
text:
Theorem, a partial result. Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero with the trivial valuation, X an integral projective unibranch k-curve, and L an ample line bundle of degree V>0 on actual X. Integrality retains reducedness and connectedness; the field is complete. Use the canonical trivial metric and normalized intersection energy E(0)=0, E(φ+c)=E(φ)+c. No smoothness or normality of X, reducedness of its conductor, atomicity or skeletal support is assumed. The genuine raw finite-energy MA has mass V and induces a bijection E¹(X,L)/R onto positive Radon μ satisfying μ(X^an)=V and E*(μ/V)=sup_{φ∈E¹}(E(φ)−V⁻¹∫φ dμ)<∞. The published background is precisely scoped in n1.

Normalization and PL descent. The normalization ν:Y→X is finite; Y is smooth because k is perfect and Y is a normal curve. Properness centers every valuation of the common function field. At a closed point q of Y the local DVR makes every nontrivial valuation t ord_q, t>0. The other analytic points are the common trivial root o and closed-support endpoints q∞. Unibranchness gives one q over each p∈X(k), with residue field k. Thus ν^an bijects both generic-support valuations and endpoints. Compactness of the source and Hausdorffness of the target make it a homeomorphism.

Let m_p O_{Y,q}=m_q^{e_p}, where 1≤e_p<∞. Away from q the extended point ideal is the unit ideal. For rational a>0, the actual-X flag-ideal function h_{p,a}=e_p⁻¹ max(log|m_p|,−e_p a) pulls back to −min(t,a) on the q-ray and zero on every other ray. It belongs to PL(X) by BJ Example 2.5. These functions and rational constants span PL(Y) by Example 2.6. Hence ν* identifies PL(X) with PL(Y), also over R. The conductor Ann(ν_*O_Y/O_X) has finite support and may be nonreduced. No arbitrary section or power descent is used; e_p is the point-ideal order, not a conductor exponent. The single branch is essential to this isolated-ray identity.

Polarization and positivity. The quotient in 0→O_X→ν_*O_Y→T→0 has finite length. Tensoring by L^m and comparing linear coefficients of χ(Y,(ν*L)^m) and χ(X,L^m) proves deg_Y ν*L=V. Positive degree on a projective integral curve is ample, so the upstairs polarization is genuinely ample, with no mass multiplier. Canonical reference metrics pull back through local trivializations at centers.

For a descended PL function, the graph construction gives a projective surjective morphism of test configurations. Pullback preserves nefness. Conversely each vertical curve downstairs is dominated by a curve upstairs, obtained by projective hyperplane cuts; its pullback degree is a positive degree multiple of the downstairs degree. Thus nefness reflects. Common dominating models preserve the model-psh property. This applies BJ Proposition 3.6(vi) after PL descent has been proved. Approximate any psh function on Y decreasingly by H_dom(Y,ν*L). Its PL approximants descend and are nef-psh on actual X; decreasing closure gives psh descent. Ordinary pullback gives the reverse inclusion. Therefore ν* is a psh-cone isomorphism and a weak homeomorphism, since divisorial valuations of the common function field are identified. No envelope property on X has been assumed.

Energy and operator. Write a=φ(o) and b_q(t)=−φ'_q(t) almost everywhere. The smooth-curve criterion, transported through the proved cone isomorphism, says b_q≥0 is nonincreasing, Σ_q b_q(0+)≤V, and φ_q(t)=a−∫₀ᵗb_q. Endpoints have limiting values, possibly −∞. Only countably many rays are nonconstant. For PL potentials the genuine raw intersection measure is Vδ_o+Δφ. Integration by parts gives E(φ)=a−D(φ)/(2V), where D(φ)=Σ_q∫₀∞b_q². Model energy projection follows from the normalization fundamental-cycle projection formula, so no conductor boundary term is omitted.

Approximate b_q increasingly from below by nonincreasing rational step functions on finitely many rays and bounded intervals, using refining dyadic right-endpoint samples and rounding down. Initial budgets stay ≤V. Their integrals give decreasing PL psh approximants, including at endpoints. Monotone energy extension and monotone convergence prove the same formula for every psh φ. Thus E¹ is exactly D(φ)<∞. Actual ample-model approximation is also available: if f_n↓φ and ||h_n−f_n||∞≤ε_n=2⁻ⁿ, the potentials h_n+3ε_n decrease with the same limit. Proposition 3.10 supplies h_n∈H_dom(X,L) in the fixed ample class.

Finite D forces b_q(∞)=0. Define MA_raw,X(φ)=(V−Σ b_q(0+))δ_o+Σ_q(−db_q)|_(0,∞), transported to actual X. Each positive Stieltjes ray measure has mass b_q(0+); total mass is exactly V and endpoints have no mass. The countable sum is Radon, with total-variation tails tending to zero. It agrees with model intersection MA and therefore with the unique published decreasing finite-energy extension, by density of actual-X PL test functions. Energy projection extends decreasingly, identifying E¹ spaces and yielding MA_raw,X(φ)=ν_*MA_raw,Y(ν*φ). This is genuine MA, not another inverse measure construction.

Measure energy and inverse. Rays minus o, including endpoints, are disjoint open subsets. A compact subset of their union meets finitely many rays; Radon inner regularity therefore concentrates any finite μ away from o on countably many rays. For raw mass V, let μ_q be its ray restriction and τ_q(t)=μ_q((t,∞]), including possible endpoint mass. Put D(μ)=Σ∫τ_q². Endpoint mass forces D(μ)=∞. Tonelli gives −∫(φ−a)dμ=Σ∫b_qτ_q. If D(μ)<∞, Cauchy–Schwarz proves integrability of every finite-energy potential. Completing the square gives E(φ)−V⁻¹∫φdμ≤D(μ)/(2V).

For the reverse inequality, use continuous psh tests with slopes τ_q 1_[0,T) on finitely many rays F and zero elsewhere. Their initial budget is ≤V, and their objective is (2V)⁻¹Σ_{q∈F}∫₀ᵀτ_q². Increasing F,T proves E*(μ/V)=D(μ)/(2V), including the infinite case. Uniform H_dom approximation of these tests, and decreasing approximation with monotone integration for E¹ tests, proves equivalence of the two suprema.

When D(μ)<∞, define φ(o)=0 and φ_q(t)=−∫₀ᵗτ_q(s)ds=−∫min(t,u)dμ_q(u), with endpoint limits. The finite F,T tests decrease to it, so it is psh on actual X. Its energy is −D(μ)/(2V). Its Stieltjes measures are μ_q and its root coefficient is μ({o}), giving MA_raw(φ)=μ. Conversely any finite-energy solution has −db_q=μ_q and b_q(∞)=0, hence b_q=τ_q. These slopes determine all values, including endpoint limits, up to the root constant. This proves necessity and uniqueness without assuming an upstairs solution descends.

Required analytic replacements. The weak normalized psh cone on actual X is homeomorphic to the smooth Y cone, compact by BJ Theorems 5.20/5.11. Analytic homeomorphism commutes with usc regularization, and the proved cone bijection identifies every envelope competitor: ν*P_X(f)=P_Y(ν*f). Envelopes and their continuity therefore descend without a circular target-envelope assumption.

The quadratic energy differentiates along E¹ segments to V⁻¹∫(ψ−φ)MA_raw(φ). BJ Theorem 8.5 gives downward-energy differentiation for actual-X PL variations without smoothness. The proved envelope property identifies downward energy with E(P(φ+tf)). Uniform PL approximation with |f−f_m|≤ε_m bounds perturbed energy errors by |t|ε_m, proving d/dt|₀ E(P(φ+tf))=V⁻¹∫f MA_raw(φ) for every continuous f. For u=P(f), P(u+t(f−u))=u when 0≤t≤1, so differentiation also proves ∫(f−u)MA_raw(u)=0.

BJ locality for finite-energy maxima applies to the identified genuine operator. Equal raw mass and locality for max(φ,ψ−ε), followed by ε↓0, give ∫_{φ<ψ}MA_raw(ψ)≤∫_{φ<ψ}MA_raw(φ). Possible negative-infinite loci here are endpoints with zero MA mass. Published decreasing continuity holds for every finite-energy approximating net, not only the selected steps; Proposition 12.7 gives strong continuity. The cone and energy identifications preserve weak-plus-energy strong potential topology and weak-plus-dual-energy strong measure topology. The completed-square bound is attained by the explicit inverse, establishing actual variational attainment.

For a continuous semipositive reference ρ, relative energy is E_ρ(φ−ρ)=E(φ)−E(ρ), by the energy cocycle and decreasing extension. Dual energy becomes E*(μ/V)−E(ρ)+V⁻¹∫ρdμ, a finite change. Thus finite energy is independent of these bounded reference changes. Integrality makes one additive real constant the correct uniqueness ambiguity.

The complete proof and residual obligations are in P16.1-argument.md and standalone P16.1-paper.tex; build/P16.1-paper.pdf has 11 pages. Run bash rerun.sh. Both actual TeX passes returned 0; the final pass has no warnings. Exact rational examples with V=5 give D(μ)=8, E(φ)=−4/5, dual objective 4/5, and both segment-derivative computations 4/5. Point-ideal orders e=1,2,3,7 give the isolated-ray identity. These are finite consistency observations, not proof verification. Actual diagnostics and outputs are in build/, curve-checks.json and checks.json. This theorem restricts dimension to one and uses the trivial field endpoint; it does not complete P16.1.

detailedSummary: On an integral projective nodal curve over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, μ=Vδ_ord(q1) has finite actual-X dual energy at most V/2 but no actual-X finite-energy solution. The unique normalization solution drops by V at one preimage of the node and by zero at the other, contradicting fiber constancy. The draft leaves higher-dimensional PL/psh/conductor descent, unibranch envelopes, the nontrivially discretely valued singular finite-energy package, and a corrected branched-measure range unresolved. Required inputs, proof files, source extracts and twice-run TeX diagnostics are retained.
text:
Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero. Let X be an integral projective curve with an ordinary node p, L ample of raw degree V, and q1,q2 its normalization preimages. Put μ=Vδ_v, where v=ord_q1 viewed on X^an. This has the exact required raw mass. Every actual-X psh potential pulls back to Y, and model projection followed by decreasing extension preserves its energy without asserting surjectivity of pullback. Therefore E*_X(δ_v)≤E*_Y(δ_ord_q1)=V/2, by n2's smooth-curve tail calculation at t=1. Thus μ has finite dual energy on actual X.

Suppose μ=MA_raw,X(φ) for φ∈E¹(X,L). Normalization pushforward identifies its upstairs MA. Normalization is injective at finite generic-support ray points, and finite-energy MA has no endpoint mass, so the upstairs measure is exactly Vδ_ord_q1. By n2's slope uniqueness, its potential is a−V min(t,1) on the q1-ray and constant a on the q2-ray. Endpoint values are a−V and a. Both endpoints map to p, whereas a pulled-back function must be constant on that fiber. This contradiction proves failure of surjectivity. No arbitrary restriction of a measure was normalized and no potential descent was assumed. This is the raw-mass obstruction of BJ Example 12.11, with the descent checked.

The positive theorem consequently retains unibranchness and integrality. On disconnected spaces, polarization masses must be fixed componentwise and uniqueness has a constant per component. On branched singular spaces, standard mass and finite energy are insufficient; a corrected measure range requires an explicit conductor-compatible theory.

The whole original atom remains unresolved in this draft. The curve generator argument does not prove higher-dimensional PL or psh descent. Topological normalization homeomorphism alone supplies none of semipositivity, approximation, energy preservation for arbitrary upstairs potentials, or envelopes. In the inspected trivial-field source, unibranch envelopes remain Conjecture 5.14, and Theorem 12.8 makes their proof the missing general existence input. This concerns the exact inspected version, not every later theorem outside the authorized caches. Pullback of an ample class to a resolution may be nonample, so no smooth ample-class theorem was silently applied there.

No singular-space finite-energy equation package is established here over the nontrivially discretely valued residue-characteristic-zero endpoint. The saved BFJ v1 algebraizability and SNC-support assumptions cannot be erased. Higher-dimensional conductor descents and a corrected admissible-measure range for non-unibranch varieties remain unsupplied.
